name: Okta — OAuth Token Reuse Detected (Session Hijack)
xql_query:
dataset = okta_sso_raw
| filter eventType = "app.oauth2.as.token.detect_reuse"
| alter user_name = arrayindex(regextract(actor, "\"alternateId\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0),
        ip = arrayindex(regextract(client, "\"ipAddress\"\s*:\s*\"([^\"]+)\""), 0)
| filter user_name != null
| filter not (user_name contains "svc-" or user_name contains "api-" or user_name contains "default.user")
| bin _time span = 30m
| comp count() as reuse_events, values(ip) as ip_list by user_name, _time
| filter reuse_events >= 1
| fields user_name, ip_list
description: Okta app.oauth2.as.token.detect_reuse event — Okta natively detected a one-time refresh token being replayed, indicating a stolen/hijacked session token.
alert_name: Okta — OAuth Token Reuse Detected (Session Hijack)
alert_description:
What fired: Okta app.oauth2.as.token.detect_reuse event — Okta natively detected a one-time refresh token being replayed, indicating a stolen/hijacked session token.

Why it matters: an actor is attempting to obtain or brute-force credentials. Assessed severity: High.

MITRE ATT&CK: T1539 - Steal Web Session Cookie (TA0006 - Credential Access); T1550.004 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie (TA0008 - Lateral Movement).

Investigate:
  - Identify the targeted account(s) and the source IP, and check for a SUCCESSFUL authentication following the failures.
  - Determine whether the source is expected; look for MFA prompts, password resets, or new sessions from the same source.
  - Pivot on the alert's key entity (user_name) to related activity in the same window.
  - Confirm the activity is not expected/authorized for the involved entity before escalating.

TA0008 - Lateral Movement: T1550.004 - Use Alternate Authentication Material: Web Session Cookie
